notice: DEMO CONTENT for the Globe News concept. These are sample stories written to show the design. They are not real, current news. Replace this file with the output of the live news pipeline.

fields.headline: story headline
fields.category: markets | companies | economy | technology | crypto | commodities | geopolitics
fields.location: place, country (as in countries-110m), lat, lon, region (na, eu, asia, me, af, latam, oc)
fields.entities: companies / assets involved: name, ticker (as the source gives it), sym (Investedia symbol in assets/quotes.js, used for the price chart and logo)
fields.links: ids of stories this one leads to (for connection arcs)
fields.source: name + original url (required for real stories)
fields.published_at: ISO time from the source (required for real stories)
fields.retrieved_at: ISO time we fetched it (required for real stories)
fields.age_minutes: DEMO ONLY: age relative to page load, used when published_at is null
fields.image: null = Investedia card (A: real price chart of the first asset with data, logo, country outline). Or an object for openly licensed photos: kind 'place' (C: the real place or institution in the story) or 'topic' (B: illustration of the subject), file or url, alt, credit, license, license_url, source, source_url. Credit and licence are always shown.

stories.headline: US cloud giants signal higher AI data-center spending
stories.summary: Large US cloud providers point to rising investment in data centers built for artificial intelligence, a key demand signal for the chip supply chain.
stories.why: Cloud providers are the biggest buyers of AI accelerators. Their spending plans feed directly into orders for chip designers, chip makers and the equipment suppliers behind them.

stories.headline: Nvidia announces new AI chips
stories.summary: Nvidia presents its next generation of data-center processors for training and running AI models.
stories.why: Nvidia designs most of the accelerators used to train large AI models. It does not manufacture them itself: production is outsourced, mainly to TSMC in Taiwan.

stories.headline: TSMC expands advanced chip packaging capacity
stories.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing adds capacity for the advanced packaging used in AI processors.
stories.why: TSMC is the world's largest contract chip maker and produces most of the leading-edge chips designed by companies like Nvidia and Apple.

image.alt: A semiconductor wafer being removed from processing equipment, illustration

stories.headline: ASML reports strong semiconductor demand
stories.summary: ASML points to solid demand for its chip-making machines, led by orders tied to advanced AI chips.
stories.why: ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography systems, the machines needed to manufacture the most advanced semiconductors.

stories.headline: Oil prices react to production decision
stories.summary: Crude prices move after producers in the OPEC+ group update their output plans.
stories.why: Saudi Arabia is one of the world's largest oil exporters and a leading member of OPEC+. Changes in the group's output can move global oil prices.

image.alt: An oil refinery at night (Mina Al-Ahmadi, Kuwait), illustration

stories.headline: Brent crude futures swing after supply news
stories.summary: The international oil benchmark trades in a wider range as traders price in the new supply outlook.
stories.why: Brent is the main global price reference for crude oil. Many fuel and energy contracts worldwide are priced from it.

stories.headline: European stocks open lower as energy costs climb
stories.summary: Major European indices start the session lower, with energy-sensitive sectors under pressure.
stories.why: Europe imports most of its oil and gas, so higher energy prices raise costs for many European companies.

stories.headline: Airline shares slip on higher fuel outlook
stories.summary: European airline stocks trade lower as investors weigh the impact of more expensive jet fuel.
stories.why: Fuel is one of an airline's largest operating costs, so oil price moves often show up quickly in airline share prices.

stories.headline: ECB decision impacts European markets
stories.summary: The European Central Bank's latest policy decision moves euro-area bond yields and the euro.
stories.why: The ECB sets interest rates for the 20 countries that use the euro, which affects borrowing costs for households, companies and governments.

image.alt: The European Central Bank tower and the Frankfurt skyline at dawn

stories.headline: EU finance ministers meet in Brussels on capital markets union
stories.summary: Finance ministers discuss plans to make it easier for companies to raise money across EU borders.
stories.why: A deeper single market for capital could change how European companies are funded and how savers invest.

stories.headline: Belgian inflation figures published
stories.summary: Belgium's statistics office releases the latest consumer price data.
stories.why: Belgium indexes most wages to inflation, so price data feeds directly into salaries and company costs.

stories.headline: AB InBev outlook in focus for European consumer stocks
stories.summary: Investors look to the world's largest brewer for signals on consumer demand.
stories.why: AB InBev, headquartered in Leuven, is one of the largest companies listed in Belgium and a bellwether for global beer demand.

stories.headline: EU stablecoin rules move to the next phase
stories.summary: European regulators publish further guidance for stablecoin issuers under the MiCA framework.
stories.why: MiCA is the EU's rulebook for crypto-assets. It decides which stablecoins can be offered to people in Europe.

stories.headline: Chinese exports beat expectations
stories.summary: China's monthly trade data shows exports growing faster than economists expected.
stories.why: China is the world's largest exporter of goods. Its trade data is watched as a signal for global demand and for commodity buyers like Australia.

stories.headline: Iron ore miners track Chinese steel demand
stories.summary: Australian miners move with expectations for steel production in China.
stories.why: Australia is the world's largest iron ore exporter, and China buys most of it to make steel.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan changes policy
stories.summary: The Bank of Japan adjusts its monetary policy settings, moving the yen and Japanese bond yields.
stories.why: Japan has kept rates very low for decades. Changes at the BoJ can move the yen and global funding flows that borrow in yen.

image.alt: The Bank of Japan head office in Tokyo

stories.headline: Samsung outlines memory chip outlook
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics comments on demand for memory chips used in AI servers and phones.
stories.why: Samsung is one of the largest memory chip makers. Memory prices are a closely watched indicator of the electronics cycle.

stories.headline: Indian equities climb as foreign inflows return
stories.summary: Foreign investors add to Indian stocks, lifting the main indices.
stories.why: India is one of the fastest-growing large economies, and foreign fund flows are a major driver of its stock market.

stories.headline: Crypto trading volumes rise on Asian exchanges
stories.summary: Trading activity in bitcoin and ether picks up during Asian trading hours.
stories.why: Crypto trades around the clock; Asian sessions often set the tone before Europe and the US open.

stories.headline: Wall Street opens mixed ahead of inflation data
stories.summary: US stocks start the day without a clear direction as investors wait for new inflation figures.
stories.why: US inflation data shapes expectations for Federal Reserve interest rates, which influence markets worldwide.

stories.headline: Tesla shares fall after earnings
stories.summary: Tesla stock trades lower after the company's quarterly results and outlook.
stories.why: Tesla is one of the largest companies in the S&P 500 by market value, so its moves can weigh on the wider index.

stories.headline: Fed officials weigh timing of next rate move
stories.summary: Speeches from Federal Reserve officials focus on how long to hold interest rates at current levels.
stories.why: The Federal Reserve sets US interest rates, the most important benchmark for global borrowing costs and the dollar.

stories.headline: Canadian dollar tracks oil and rate outlook
stories.summary: The loonie moves with crude prices and expectations for the Bank of Canada.
stories.why: Canada is a major oil exporter, so its currency often moves with energy prices.

stories.headline: Brazil central bank decision in focus
stories.summary: Markets look ahead to the next interest-rate decision from Brazil's central bank.
stories.why: Brazil has some of the highest interest rates among large economies, which strongly affects the real and local stocks.

stories.headline: Nearshoring lifts Mexican manufacturing investment
stories.summary: Companies continue to expand factories in northern Mexico to serve the US market.
stories.why: Mexico is the United States' largest trading partner, and factory investment there shapes trade and the peso.

stories.headline: Copper output update from Chilean mines
stories.summary: Production figures from major Chilean copper mines are released.
stories.why: Chile is the world's largest copper producer. Copper is used in wiring, electric vehicles and power grids.

stories.headline: South African rand moves with metals prices
stories.summary: The rand tracks prices of the metals South Africa exports.
stories.why: South Africa is a leading producer of platinum and gold, so metals prices strongly influence its currency.

stories.headline: Nigeria fuel price changes ripple through the economy
stories.summary: Changes to fuel pricing feed into transport and food costs across Nigeria.
stories.why: Nigeria is Africa's largest oil producer and one of its biggest economies; fuel prices affect inflation and the naira.

stories.headline: Suez Canal traffic in focus for shipping costs
stories.summary: Shipping companies watch transit volumes through the Suez Canal.
stories.why: Around a tenth of world trade normally passes through the Suez Canal. Diversions add time and cost to shipments between Asia and Europe.

image.alt: A container ship passing through the Suez Canal

stories.headline: Aramco updates crude prices for Asian buyers
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco publishes its monthly official selling prices for crude shipped to Asia.
stories.why: Aramco is the world's largest oil company, and its monthly prices are a reference for Asian refiners.

stories.headline: Dubai hosts sovereign wealth investment forum
stories.summary: Gulf sovereign funds discuss investment plans at a forum in Dubai.
stories.why: Gulf sovereign wealth funds manage some of the largest pools of capital in the world and invest across global markets.

stories.headline: RBA keeps watch on housing and inflation
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia's latest minutes focus on housing costs and inflation.
stories.why: The RBA sets interest rates for Australia, where many home loans have variable rates that react quickly to its decisions.

stories.headline: Swiss franc strengthens as investors seek safety
stories.summary: The franc gains as investors move money into assets seen as safer.
stories.why: The Swiss franc is traditionally considered a safe-haven currency during market stress.

stories.headline: German carmakers weigh electric-vehicle pricing
stories.summary: Germany's large carmakers review pricing for electric models in Europe and China.
stories.why: Car manufacturing is one of Germany's largest industries and a big part of the DAX index.

stories.headline: UK inflation data due; gilts steady
stories.summary: UK government bonds trade calmly ahead of the next inflation release.
stories.why: UK inflation figures guide Bank of England rate decisions and mortgage costs.

stories.headline: Norway's wealth fund reports quarterly results
stories.summary: The world's largest sovereign wealth fund publishes its latest quarterly return.
stories.why: Norway's fund owns a small stake in thousands of listed companies worldwide, making it one of the largest single investors in global stocks.
